items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: And Brodsky on piano. All fine, superb musicians who could...

ctx.x: And Brodsky on piano. All fine, superb musicians who could... In fact, that band was known to the music publishers, which is a great tribute, as the band for the okaying of their arrangements. They'd come up with a manuscript, and the boys would put it on the stand and read it and knock it right off. No rehearsal whatsoever. That's a band that can do that, you know. No rehearsal. And then we'd cut it up, and we'd take solo parts here and give it to Red. We'd make a modulation here for Rilini, and ideas would…

This was about ten years after the original Dixieland jazz band played New York, or seven or eight years anyway. And by this time, the boys had begun to either get other influences or show a great deal of originality. They were using the original New Orleans jazz as a background, but they were beginning to show a little independence on phrasing.
